toegepas.voor: weggevee of hou hulle in toom
toegepas.na: weggevee, of dit hou hulle in toom
toegepas.rede_vinder: The second verb shifts tense without its own subject; repeating the subject makes the two options read as two clear clauses and needs the AWS comma before 'of'.
toegepas.fout: The perfect 'het ... weggevee' and the present 'hou' share one subject across 'of', so a reader can stumble by reading 'het ... hou' together.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Repeating the subject makes two clear clauses with the same meaning and the same referent (the planet), and the comma before 'of' is the required AWS comma.

laat_vaar.voor: ruimte met die asteroïdes ver van mekaar af
laat_vaar.na: ruimte, en die asteroïdes is ver van mekaar af
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The 'met ... ver van mekaar af' construction follows English 'with the asteroids far apart'; a second clause is more natural Afrikaans, and the protected wording before it stays intact.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: The absolute 'met die asteroiedes ver van mekaar af' is ordinary Afrikaans (as in 'met die deur oop'), so splitting it into a second clause is a lateral move that also loosens the link between the empty space and the spacing.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Parallel with 'Ons noem hulle die rotsagtige planete' in the same block; the protected word 'gasplanete' is unchanged.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Ons noem hulle gasplanete' is a natural naming sentence, so adding 'die' to match the earlier sentence is only a different wording, not a better one.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Die gordel skei so die rotsagtige planete
laat_vaar_vorige.na: So skei die gordel die rotsagtige planete
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'so' in the middle of the clause reads awkwardly; fronting it gives natural word order.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Die gordel skei so ...' is normal Afrikaans word order, so fronting 'So' is a lateral move.
